title: Chapter 116 — The Dying Whale
paragraphs: It happens often enough in this life that when fortune's favorites sail close by us on the right side, we, though we were drooping before, catch something of their rushing breeze and joyfully feel our slack sails fill out. So it seemed with the Pequod. On the day after she met the cheerful Bachelor, whales were sighted and four were killed, one of them by Ahab.

It was far into the afternoon; and when all the spearings of the crimson fight were done, and, floating in the lovely sunset sea and sky, sun and whale both silently died together — then such sweetness and such plaintiveness, such wreathing prayers, curled up into that rosy air that it almost seemed as if, far over from the deep green convent valleys of the Manila isles, the Spanish land-breeze, wantonly turned sailor, had gone to sea freighted with these vesper hymns.

Soothed again, but only soothed to deeper gloom, Ahab, who had backed off from the whale, sat intently watching its final wanings from the now tranquil boat. For that strange spectacle observable in all sperm whales dying — the turning sunward of the head, and so expiring — that strange spectacle, seen on such a placid evening, somehow conveyed to Ahab a wondrousness unknown before.

"He turns and turns himself to it — how slowly, but how steadfastly, his homage-rendering and invoking brow, with his last dying motions. He too worships fire; most faithful, broad, baronial vassal of the sun! Oh, that these too-favoring eyes should see these too-favoring sights. Look! Here, far water-locked; beyond all hum of human weal or woe; in these most candid and impartial seas; where no rocks furnish tablets for traditions; where for long Chinese ages the billows have still rolled on speechless and unspoken to, like stars that shine upon the Niger's unknown source — here, too, life dies sunward full of faith; but see! No sooner dead than death whirls round the corpse, and it heads some other way.

"Oh, you dark Hindu half of nature, who have built your separate throne of drowned bones somewhere in the heart of these unverdured seas; you are an infidel, you queen, and too truly you speak to me in the wide-slaughtering Typhoon, and the hushed burial of its after-calm. Nor has this whale of yours turned his dying head sunward, and then gone round again, without a lesson to me.

"Oh, trebly hooped and welded hip of power! Oh, high aspiring, rainbowed jet! The one strives, the other jets, all in vain! In vain, oh whale, do you seek intercession with the all-quickening sun, that only calls forth life but does not give it again. Yet you, darker half, rock me with a prouder, if a darker faith. All your unnamable imminglings float beneath me here; I am buoyed by breaths of once living things, exhaled as air, but water now.

"Then hail, forever hail, O sea, in whose eternal tossing the wild bird finds its only rest. I was born of earth, yet nursed by the sea; though hill and valley mothered me, you rolling waves are my foster-brothers!"
